A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material that was relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations, humanization experiments, supervised classification results and human validation of the content judge.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments with Grammarly edits, back-translated reviews and personalized polishing instructions in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The context-conditioned detectors, reference-similarity classifiers, stylometric classifier and RoBERTa procedure are unchanged. The additional polishing workflows generate evaluation inputs rather than modify the proposed detection methods.

E1.justification: Appendix B extends coverage to Grammarly proofreading, translation-assisted reviews through German, Chinese and Japanese, and personalized polishing. These are focused scenario extensions using the existing review corpus; the translation experiments use synthetic proxies rather than authentic non-English reviews.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same five off-the-shelf detectors and the same contextual, similarity-based and supervised comparisons. Grammarly, Google Translate and DeepL generate test inputs; they are not new detection baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include accepting all Grammarly suggestions on 100 randomly sampled reviews, using different translators for forward and backward translation, and adding stylistic instructions. Section 3 revises the reported easy/hard subset sizes from 18,340/27,429 to 18,122/26,535, reconciling the total with 50,156 after humanization. The PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds focused robustness checks asking whether false positives persist across alternative policy-compliant writing workflows. The existing prompt-safeguard analysis, held-out-model tests, humanization study, judge validation and review examples remain, with some relocated.

E5.justification: The Cohen's kappa confidence intervals and 50-pair judge validation are unchanged, as are the McNemar testing procedures and significance reporting. The new polishing experiments introduce no new repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Appendix B newly reports zero fully-AI labels among 100 Grammarly-edited reviews, translation false-positive rates of 1.1–4.5% in Table 9, and 2.42% for personalized polishing, all from Pangram. Existing main result tables retain their values. The stylometric H-AI false-positive rate in the prose is corrected from 6.4% to 4.3%, matching the table already present in v1.

T1.justification: The statistical formulas, similarity definitions and stylometric feature definitions are retained. The new discussion of correlated detection errors across paper windows is a qualitative applicability argument, not a new formal assumption, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claim about current detectors' inability to reliably enforce polishing-only policies. The introduction extends the false-positive finding to translation and personalized polishing while explicitly identifying Grammarly-style edits as an exception.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the applicability and policy discussion. The introduction explains why review-level false-positive rates cannot be extrapolated to whole papers without evidence about correlated window errors. Appendix E distinguishes detector outputs from broader enforcement mechanisms and qualifies blanket-ban enforceability through productivity costs and untested adaptive evasion. Appendix B also acknowledges non-exhaustive coverage of private polishing practices.

D1.justification: Appendix B documents the manual Grammarly Proofreader workflow, identifies the Google Cloud Translate and DeepL interfaces, and specifies the added stylistic instructions. Existing detector versions, embedding configurations, generation prompts and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning rigorous reviewer evaluation, Pangram false positives, ICLR enforcement and NeurIPS paper screening, including Baumann et al., Emi and Lu et al. These broaden practical positioning without replacing the main research framing. Publication updates to existing works, including the AI Review Lottery reference, are not new cited research.

P1.justification: Humanization is moved ahead of the contextual-detection experiments, the appendices are reorganized, and an appendix contents list is added. Validation and content-addition examples are grouped together, with local wording, citation and front-matter edits. Most existing prose and prompts remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the translation-results table and changes placement and text wrapping around existing displays. The humanization table moves from Table 6 to Table 3, and appendix tables are relocated or relabeled. The five existing figures retain their plotted content and visual designs.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens the empirical checks, clarifies limits on full-paper extrapolation and adversarial enforcement, and fixes inconsistent dataset totals and a prose result. These improve the paper's precision while retaining its core evidence. The gain is limited by the small Grammarly study: observing no fully-AI labels in 100 reviews does not establish the zero-risk language used in Appendix B.
